channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: US Deportation Plans for Afghans Halted Amid Advocacy and Legal Challenges
item.description: Dozens of Afghans facing deportation from the US to Afghanistan have experienced relief as plans to remove them appear to be on hold. A flight scheduled for election day was grounded by a court order. Advocates warn deportations could be a death sentence, with a rescheduled date looming for some detainees.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Gas Supply for Residential and Social Facilities This Winter
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved gas distribution plans for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter season, prioritizing residential homes, schools, kindergartens, and hospitals. Supply may be temporarily restricted for other consumers during severe cold spells to ensure uninterrupted service for priority users.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Proposes Announcing Utility Tariff Changes Years in Advance
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has proposed announcing the schedule of changes in utility tariffs several years in advance. This proposal is part of the draft main directions of monetary policy for 2027-2029. The document notes that the increase in prices for some fuel types and regulated services exceeded initial expectations.

item.title: Zelensky: Putin Seeks to Redefine European Borders; Warns of Threats to Finland, Sweden, Baltics
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that Putin aims to redefine European borders and identified Finland, Sweden, and Baltic states as countries under threat. He also mentioned that Americans proposed the idea of the US giving territory to Russia in exchange for Ukraine's NATO membership.

item.title: Taliban Arrest Panjshir Man Returning from Iran, Accused of Cooperating with Resistance Front
item.description: Sources report that the Taliban arrested a young man named Ahmad Zabur from Panjshir province about a month ago while he was returning from Iran. He is accused of cooperating with the National Resistance Front. His family has no information about his whereabouts or detention location.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General Investigates Personal Data Leaks and Cybersecurity Committee
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office is conducting a comprehensive review of the Cybersecurity Committee's operations. The investigation focuses on the legality of collecting, storing, and transferring citizens' personal data and the adequacy of protection measures. The probe also examines Yandex service failures and the public release of personal data from educational institutions.

item.title: Afghan Girls Face Continued Oppression and Denial of Education Under Taliban Rule
item.description: Over five years after the Taliban's return, Afghan girls remain deprived of education, with schools and universities closed to them. Their dreams of progress through learning are shattered by the regime's restrictions, confining their activities to their homes. The prolonged denial of education significantly impacts their lives, youth, and aspirations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Seizes Nearly 1.8 kg of Drugs Smuggled from Afghanistan
item.description: Uzbek authorities in the Surkhandarya region have intercepted a smuggling attempt involving nearly 1.8 kilograms of narcotics from Afghanistan. Drugs were found hidden in vehicle parts, including an engine piston containing approximately 400 grams of opium. Further investigation led to the arrest of a suspected recipient in Denov district.

item.title: Man Suspected of Extremism Propaganda Arrested in Almaty After Receiving 60 Million Tenge
item.description: A 44-year-old man suspected of promoting religious extremism and inciting religious hatred has been arrested in Almaty. He allegedly administered closed Telegram groups and conducted online lectures from abroad since 2024, receiving over 60 million tenge from followers.

item.title: Kyrgyz Ambassador to Japan Replaced; New Envoy Appointed
item.description: Urmat Toktogulov has been appointed as the new Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Japan, replacing Erkinbek Osoev. Osoev had served as ambassador since January 2023 and previously held the position of Minister of Transport and Communications.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Attends 'World Atomic Days' Forum in Antalya
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan participated in the 'World Atomic Days' forum held in Antalya on November 12-13. The event, organized by Rosatom, focused on the development of nuclear energy, energy diversification, and technological advancements. Discussions included nuclear energy's role in energy security, sustainable development, and climate change mitigation.

item.title: Tashkent Identifies Districts with Highest HIV Detection Rates
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, Tashkent recorded 307 new HIV cases, a decrease of 17 from the previous year. Bektemir district reported the highest detection rate at 17 cases per 100,000 population. The majority of new infections were sexually transmitted. The Tashkent City Council urged the health department to enhance HIV prevention efforts.

item.title: Tashkent Sees Rise in Mental Health Patients, With Children Forming Nearly Half of New Cases
item.description: Tashkent registered nearly 2,700 new mental health patients in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 269 from the previous year. Notably, children constitute almost half of these new cases, with 1,300 minors diagnosed. The city's health department has been tasked with improving mental health services.

item.title: US Pentagon Blocks License for Ukraine to Produce Patriot Missiles
item.description: The US Pentagon has blocked the issuance of a license for Ukraine to produce Patriot missile components. Despite prior agreement from the Secretary of State and Secretary of Defense, the final approval is stalled at the Under Secretary of Defense level. The move comes amid Ukraine's critical shortage of Patriot interceptor missiles.

item.title: Almaty Airport Completes Renovation of Domestic Flights Terminal
item.description: Almaty Airport has finished a major upgrade of its domestic flights terminal (T1). The renovation included updated check-in and security zones, baggage infrastructure, and waiting areas. Officials stated the upgrade aims to enhance passenger comfort and strengthen Almaty's role as a regional transport hub.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India to Enhance Control Over Quality and Safety of Medicines
item.description: Uzbekistan and India will strengthen control over the quality and safety of medicinal products. During a scientific expedition to India, specialists from Uzbekistan reached significant agreements in pharmaceuticals and standardization. A memorandum of cooperation was signed with Jamia Hamdard University in Delhi.

item.title: 3.5 Hectares of Agricultural Land in Osh Allocated for Housing Construction
item.description: In Osh, 3.5 hectares of irrigated agricultural land have been reclassified for the construction of a multi-story residential complex with social facilities. The decision, signed by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, allows for the development of two state-owned plots previously used for farming. This is an exception to the moratorium on transforming irrigated land.

item.title: Astana Hosts Conference on Digital Tools and 'Law and Order' Principle
item.description: An international scientific-practical conference on the role of digital tools in implementing the 'Law and Order' principle was held in Astana. Participants discussed modern technologies for strengthening legality, protecting citizens' rights, and combating crime. The aim was to exchange international experience and develop practical recommendations.

item.title: US First Proposed NATO Membership for Ukraine in Exchange for Donbas Withdrawal, Says Zelensky
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the US first proposed NATO membership for Ukraine in exchange for withdrawing from Donbas. He clarified that while Ukraine is discussing a comprehensive security package with partners, no specific offer of this nature has been made yet. Zelensky emphasized that any such proposal would be subject to public discussion.

item.title: Uzbek Official Attends Discussion on Future of US University and AI in Education
item.description: Kamil Allamjonov, a representative of the Uzbek Presidential Administration in the US, participated in discussions about the future development of George Washington University and higher education's prospects amidst artificial intelligence. He attended a meeting of the university's presidential advisory board.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways Expresses Readiness to Assist Investigation into Executive Detentions
item.description: Kazakhstan Railways (KTZ) has acknowledged the detention of its chairman, Yeldas Otunshiyev, and Samruk-Kazyna head, Nurlan Zhakupov, as part of a pre-trial investigation. The company stated its readiness to cooperate with law enforcement agencies and provide necessary information. KTZ confirmed that its operations and obligations remain unaffected.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Named Among World's 500 Most Influential Muslims
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has been included in the 2027 list of the world's 500 most influential Muslims by the Royal Islamic Strategic Studies Centre. He is recognized in the 'Politics' category for his leadership and reform agenda. Singer Dimash Kudaibergen also represents Kazakhstan in the 'Arts and Culture' category.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Pledging Municipal Property Without Local Council Approval
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a bill to allow local governments to pledge municipal property for national investment projects without prior consent from local councils (kenešes). The executive body would decide, but must notify the council within 10 days. This aims to expedite project implementation and boost regional investment.

item.title: Uzbekistan Negotiates 'One Stop' Border System with Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Uzbekistan is in talks with Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan to launch a unified 'One Stop' customs supervision system at select border crossings. This system aims to streamline cargo checks, potentially allowing for mutual recognition of customs procedures and data exchange, thus avoiding repeated inspections.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Orders Fair Resolution of Land Disputes in Issyk-Kul
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has instructed prosecutors and courts to thoroughly investigate land disputes in the Issyk-Kul region and protect the rights of bona fide purchasers. He emphasized distinguishing between illegal land seizures and legitimate purchases, urging fair decisions for those who invested in construction legally.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Clearer Rules for Business Closures by Health Services
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a bill to establish clear criteria for when sanitary-epidemiological services can suspend business operations. The proposed law aims to allow closures only when there's a direct threat to life or health, detailing specific violations and requiring written justifications for such decisions.

item.title: New Border Post and Housing Complex Opened in Kyrgyzstan's Osh Region
item.description: A new border post named "Intymak" (Kempir-Abad) has been opened in the Osh region of Kyrgyzstan. A 20-apartment service house was also handed over to border guards at the "Kara-Shybak" outpost in the Chon-Alay district. The housing was built using the national budget to provide modern living conditions for border guards and their families.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Natural Gas for Population in Winter 2026-2027
item.description: Uzbekistan's Cabinet of Ministers has decreed that during the 2026-2027 autumn-winter period, natural gas resources will be primarily allocated to the population, social facilities, and strategically important consumers. The decree aims to ensure stable gas supplies from October 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027, with flexible adjustments possible.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Forecasts Economic Growth for 2027-2029
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has prepared a draft on the main directions of monetary policy for 2027 and 2028-2029. The document includes a baseline forecast, external economic situation, inflation dynamics, and alternative scenarios. Economic activity is expected to approach potential levels after 2026.

item.title: Afghan Finance Minister Visits Iran for Economic Discussions
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Finance, Mohammad Nasir Akhund, is in Iran for an official visit at the invitation of Iran's Minister of Agriculture. Discussions will focus on bilateral economic, trade, and customs issues, as well as preparations for a joint economic commission meeting.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches National Cargo Airline, Alatau Air Cargo
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a national cargo airline, Alatau Air Cargo, which plans to expand its fleet to ten aircraft. The airline aims to compete with major international players and is preparing for its first commercial flights in early next year, focusing on securing clients.

item.title: Three-Year-Old Murder Case Solved in Abay Region
item.description: Police in the Abay Region have solved a murder committed over three years ago. The suspect, who was serving time for another crime, confessed to the murder after investigators pursued new leads. The suspect has indicated the location where the victim's body was hidden.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Discuss Border Crossings Using ID Cards
item.description: Diplomats from Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan met in Tashkent to discuss simplifying travel between the two nations. A key topic was the potential for citizens to cross the border using national ID cards instead of passports. The meeting also touched upon employment for Uzbek citizens in Kazakhstan and the QazETA electronic entry system.

item.title: UNHCR Representative Urges Support for Afghanistan for Global Stability
item.description: Arafat Jamal, UNHCR representative in Afghanistan, emphasizes that supporting the country is an investment in global stability, not just humanitarian aid. He urges continued support from South Korea, highlighting Afghanistan's strategic importance and the potential international consequences of neglect. Many returnees face challenges.

item.title: Tashkent Reports 35-Fold Increase in Meningococcal Infections, 24 Deaths
item.description: Tashkent has recorded 354 cases of meningococcal infection in the first nine months of 2026, a 35-fold increase from the previous year, resulting in 24 deaths, mostly children. Health authorities are investigating the surge and implementing preventive measures, including vaccination for contacts.

item.title: AI Developer Anthropic Eyes Up to $1.4 Trillion Valuation in Upcoming IPO
item.description: AI firm Anthropic, creator of the Claude chatbot, is preparing for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) with a potential valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. Investors have shown significant demand, with interest reportedly six times the available shares. The company plans to offer 825 million shares at prices between $70 and $78 each, aiming for a total offering of up to $64.4 billion.

item.title: Rehabilitated Power Line in Faryab Province to Benefit 60,000 Consumers
item.description: Afghanistan's Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar, inaugurated a rehabilitated 110 kV power transmission line in Faryab province. The project is expected to provide stable electricity to approximately 60,000 consumers, support industrial activities, and contribute to economic and social development. The Islamic Emirate aims to reduce reliance on imported electricity.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways CEO Detained Amid Corruption Investigation
item.description: Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) National Company has stated that its operations continue as normal following the detention of its CEO, Yerzhas Otynshiyev, on suspicion of corruption. The company assured investors, creditors, and partners that all obligations will be met. Information regarding the pre-trial investigation remains confidential as per the Criminal Procedure Code.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways Assures Investors of Continued Commitment After Chairman's Detention
item.description: Kazakhstan Railways (KTZ) stated it is operating normally following the detention of its chairman, Yeldjas Otinshev. The company affirmed that all obligations to investors, creditors, and partners remain unchanged. KTZ is cooperating with law enforcement agencies in the ongoing investigation.

item.title: ICC Partially Suspends Afghanistan War Crimes Investigation, Appeals Filed
item.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has partially suspended its investigation into alleged war crimes in Afghanistan, including those involving US forces and IS-K. The court's prosecution has appealed this decision, while investigations into other alleged crimes in the country will continue separately.
